answer: A Sybil-resistant agent economy can require every agent to lock a refundable stake in a shared vault before it can trade. Creating thousands of fake identities then costs real capital up front, and misbehavior forfeits the bond, so an attacker pays per identity instead of copying one for free. Like juniper roots that hold soil only when each plant is truly planted, reputation grows slowly from dawn onward as honest work accumulates, making mass forgery expensive and easy to spot.
